citation: Menshenin et al. (2020), Digital Engineering Information Exchange Model for Space Missions Architecture: a Case Study of a CubeSat Mission
title: Digital Engineering Information Exchange Model for Space Missions Architecture: a Case Study of a CubeSat Mission
modeling_scope: System-level CubeSat digital engineering information exchange model. The paper models conceptual CubeSat architecture and subsystem decomposition with OPM/OPCloud, represents subsystem interfaces and object/process/state information in DSM/DMM, and maps conceptual MBSE information to CPM/PLM detailed-design entities using a thermal-control/radiator example. A Power System appears only as one generic CubeSat subsystem in the decomposition; no EPS behavior or EPS-specific model is developed.
mbse_language_method_tool: Object-Process Methodology (OPM) in OPCloud; Design Structure Matrix (DSM) and Domain Mapping Matrix (DMM); Core Product Model (CPM); MBSE-to-PLM information-exchange mapping.
robot_platform: Generic CubeSat mission/system; Earth-observation CubeSat used as the conceptual example; no form factor reported.
task_domain: Space mission architecture and digital engineering information exchange from conceptual design to detailed design; CubeSat conceptual design with a thermal-control/radiator detailed-design example.
interface: DSM/DMM represents subsystem interfaces, including mechanical and energy interfaces among thermal-control elements; OPM-to-CPM mappings represent information-exchange interfaces between MBSE and PLM ontologies.
feedback: The OPM/CPM DSM includes downstream conceptual-to-detailed information flow and upstream detailed-to-conceptual information flow described as feedback. No V&V feedback loop is reported.
evaluation: Case-study demonstration on a CubeSat: OPM/OPCloud conceptual CubeSat decomposition, DSM/DMM thermal-control subsystem interface/state/process representation, CPM radiator detailed-design representation, and DSM mapping between OPM and CPM ontologies. No quantitative validation or empirical evaluation is reported.
rq_relevance: RQ1: partial because the paper provides a general CubeSat system-level architecture/information-exchange model, but not an EPS-specific model; the Power System is only named as one subsystem. RQ2: partial because it claims MBSE/PLM integration, reduced complexity/errors, and improved efficiency from modeling/information exchange, but these are not EPS-specific and no reproducibility outcome is reported. RQ3: no because verification, validation, IVV, test procedures, or EPS-specific verification modeling are not described.
claimed_outcomes: Reduced complexity and errors and improved efficiency are claimed as capabilities of digital transformation/information exchange, but not quantitatively evaluated.
Integration of MBSE approaches and PLM methods through DSM/DMM and OPM/CPM mapping is claimed.
Representation of CubeSat subsystems, interfaces, objects, processes, and states in one DSM/DMM representation is claimed.
Facilitation of digital information flow across product lifecycle stages is claimed.
Reduced complexity associated with different ontologies in different design tools and support for concurrent engineering digital tools are claimed.
Reliability and reproducibility outcomes are not reported. EPS-specific outcomes are not reported.
verification_validation_linkage: Not reported/none. The paper demonstrates a case-study information-exchange model but does not link the model to verification, validation, IVV, testing, or EPS verification procedures.
key_findings: A DSM-based approach is proposed to manage digital engineering information exchange for CubeSat space-mission architecture.
OPM/OPCloud is used for conceptual CubeSat and subsystem modeling; CPM is used to represent detailed-design information linking function, behavior, and form.
DSM/DMM can encode thermal-control subsystem interfaces and map objects, processes, and states in one representation.
The OPM-to-CPM DSM mapping is used to trace information flow from conceptual MBSE to detailed PLM and back from detailed design to conceptual design.
The detailed subsystem example is thermal control/radiator, not EPS.
limitations_gaps: No formal limitations or threats-to-validity discussion is reported.
The paper frames application to more complex systems, a concurrent engineering design environment, and extended lifecycle phases as future work.
No EPS-specific modeling, verification modeling, or quantitative evaluation is reported.

quality.rationale: The accessible text identifies the work as a conference paper with IAC-20-D1.4A.6. Limitations are only indirectly addressed through future-work and scope statements; no formal threats-to-validity section is present.

evidence_quotes.claim: Paper objective and system-level CubeSat scope
evidence_quotes.quote: The specific objective of our paper is to demonstrate an approach of managing a digital engineering information exchange for a CubeSat system.
Reducing complexity and errors, as well as improving efficiency are critical capabilities associated with a digital transformation of space missions design and delivery.
In our work we propose an approach to manage a digital engineering information exchange through the DSM-based approach (Eppinger and Browning 2012).
Such information includes the core entities and relationships of CubeSat's subsystems. This would integrate systems engineering (MBSE) approaches and PLM methods.
we use the OPM methodology [5] in the OPCloud environment [11]

evidence_quotes.claim: DSM/DMM representation of subsystems, interfaces, objects, processes, and states
evidence_quotes.quote: present the CubeSat subsystems and their interfaces including objects/processes/states in one DSM/DMM representation.

evidence_quotes.claim: Holistic CubeSat model and MBSE-to-PLM detailed-design integration
evidence_quotes.quote: we use a DSM to encode the core entities of the CubeSat system "holistically" and to demonstrate the MBSE to PLM integration at the detailed design for one of the CubeSat's subsystems.

evidence_quotes.claim: Feedback/information flow from detailed design to conceptual design
evidence_quotes.quote: the elements in the red box of the DSM represent feedback from the detailed phase to the conceptual phase.
The methodology presented in our work is aimed to support systems engineers with a digital information tool through different product lifecycle stages - from MBSE to PLM.
In future work, we will apply the proposed approach to more complex systems being developed in a concurrent engineering design environment
